# PLAN — iteration 4
## Current state assessment

The verified incumbent is already timing-feasible at 7 LUTs and 9 FFs, so iteration 4 must strictly reduce LUTs (or hold LUTs at 7 and reduce FFs) to improve the `minimize_luts` objective. The three prior counter-width and counter-organization proposals were rejected with 9–10 LUTs; timing recovery is not applicable. The top’s numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required.

## Hypothesis

Writing the 8-bit modulo increment as explicit carry-toggle equations may let Vivado map the counter update with fewer LUTs while preserving its 256-cycle sequence and registered PWM output.

## Instruction for generator

Keep the `pwm` interface and synchronous active-high reset behavior, and retain the registered `pwm_out <= (counter < duty)` behavior. Replace the counter’s terminal-count branch and `counter + 1` update with an 8-bit counter whose bit 0 toggles each active cycle and whose bit *i* toggles when all lower counter bits are 1, so it wraps naturally from 255 to 0; clear it on reset. Do not add pipeline stages or a numeric latency annotation; the candidate still must pass the frozen simulation and all routed metric, setup, and hold gates, and it improves the incumbent only if LUTs decrease or LUTs remain 7 with fewer FFs.
